# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll explore the codebase to find the statement labeling logic and the edge-case faults described in the forum digest.

# Bank Statement Labeling — Codebase Map

## Architecture overview

This is a Flask service (`categorizationapp`) that enriches bank transactions. Pipeline (per bank) in `Controller.categorizeTransaction`:

1. **Bank script** → `transactionCategory`, initial `partyName` / `transactionSubcategory` / `merchantType`
2. **`purpose()`** → purpose sub-tags (salary, loan, shopping, bounce subtypes, etc.)
3. **`clean_names()`** → normalize merchant/payee display names
4. **`internal_payment()`** → self-transfers via fuzzy name match
5. **`salary_detection()`** (SAVING only) → frequency/clustering salary heuristics
6. Optional **`pfm_categorization()`** + **`simple_description()`**

Default category when nothing matches is almost always **`TRANSFER`**.

There are **no test files** in the repo.

---

## Relevant source files

### Orchestration
| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | HTTP API; bank dispatch + pipeline order |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py` | Flask app bootstrap |

### Shared utilities
| Path | Key functions | Role |
|------|---------------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | `clean_input_df`, `sep_by_`, `sep_by_dash`, `py_extract`, `fuzzy_match` | Narration splitters (`/`, `-`, `:`, etc.) and regex extract |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | `SALARY`, `NOT_SAL`, `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`, `INSUFF_BOUNCE`, merchant regexes | Shared keyword rules |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | Bank-specific patterns, `TRF_STOP_WORDS`, cheque/FT patterns | Per-bank narration patterns |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` | `purpose()` | Subcategory + merchantType from party/description |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | `clean_names()` | Canonical payee names (~2k lines of merchant maps) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` | `salary_detection()` | Clustering + frequency salary labeling |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` | `internal_payment()` | Self-payment sub-tag |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` | `pfm_categorization()` | PFM L1/L2 buckets |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py` | `simple_description()` | Human-readable summary |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RecurrentTxns.py` | `recurrent_transactions()` | Recurrence endpoint |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py` / `CardCleanNames.py` | CC path | Credit-card purpose/names |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` | Category display labels |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` | Subcategory display labels |

### Bank parsers (category + counterparty extraction)
All under `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/`:

`HDFC.py`, `ICICI.py`, `Axis.py`, `SBI.py`, `Kotak.py`, `Canara.py`, `BOB.py`, `PNB.py`, `YES.py`, `Indusind.py`, `IDBI.py`, `IDFC.py`, `UnionBank.py`, `StandardCharted.py`, `Citi.py`, `RBL.py`, `Federal.py`, `Bandhan.py`, `BOI.py`, `Andhra.py`, `Karnataka.py`, `KarurVyasa.py`, `CityUnion.py`, `BankOfMaharashtra.py`, `UCO.py`, `SouthIndian.py`, `Saraswat.py`, `SVC.py`, `TamilnadMerchantile.py`, `Syndicate.py`, `Central.py`, `DCB.py`, `Paytm.py`, `AuSmallFinanceBank.py`, `Indian.py`

Most important for the four bugs: **HDFC, ICICI, Axis, SBI, Kotak, PNB, YES, UCO, RBL, BankOfMaharashtra, Saraswat, StandardCharted**.

### Tests
**None found** (`**/test*`, `**/*test*` empty).

---

## How labeling works

### 1. Bank-level category (`transactionCategory`)
Each `categorize_<Bank>_transactions()` builds ordered `conditions_choices` lists and applies them with `np.select`. First true condition wins. Typical order:

- Opening balance, verification, cashback, refunds  
- Explicit **reversals** (UPI/IMPS/ATM/charges)  
- Penalties, charges  
- **Bounce** keywords / NACH return  
- Channel: UPI, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, ACH, POS, ATM  
- Cheque paid/deposit  
- Default → **`TRANSFER`**

### 2. Counterparty (`partyName` / `party2`)
Still in the bank script: split narration with `sep_by_` (slash), `sep_by_dash`, `py_extract`, then strip noise. `party2` = spaceless `partyName` for matching.

### 3. Purpose sub-tags (`Purpose.purpose`)
Regex over `description` / `partyName` / `party2` for SALARY, LOAN, shopping, bills, technical vs insufficient cheque bounce, etc. Also clears subcategory on bounce/penalty categories.

### 4. Name cleanup (`CleanName.clean_names`)
Huge merchant dictionary rewriting noisy party strings to brands (Airtel, Zerodha, …).

### 5. Salary detection (`SalaryDetection.salary_detection`)
Only SAVING. Clusters by party name; needs **non-empty `partyName`**, amount > 2999, excludes many categories. Frequency/mode heuristics assign SALARY / REIMBURSEMENT.

### 6. PFM
Maps category/subcategory → `pfmCategoryOne` / `pfmCategoryTwo` (TRANSFER, SALARY, REVERSAL, …).

---

## Bug-by-bug: likely locations

### Bug 1 — All-numeric credit: was cheque deposit, now generic transfer; bare numeric salary lost

**Cheque-from-numeric-remark pattern (credits):**

| File | Lines | Rule |
|------|-------|------|
| `Axis.py` | 58–59 | `remark ^[0-9]{5,6}$` → CHEQUE_PAID / CHEQUE_DEPOSIT |
| `PNB.py` | 60–61 | `remark ^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| `Kotak.py` | 65–67 | `remark ^[0-9]{3,5}$` |
| `YES.py` | 52–53 | `remark ^[0-9]{3,6}$` |
| `UCO.py` | 44–45 | same |
| `BankOfMaharashtra.py` | 73–74 | `remark ^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| `RBL.py` | 49–50 | `remark ^[0-9]{1,3}$` (very short) |
| `HDFC.py` | 100 | remark len 15 + `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT |
| `TamilnadMerchantile.py` | 33–34 | `remark ^[0-9]{5,}/` |

If remark is **long all-numeric** (or empty) and description has no CHQ/CLG keyword, nothing matches → default **`TRANSFER`**. That matches “used to show as cheque deposit, now generic transfer.”

**Salary on bare numeric narration:**

| Location | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| `Purpose.py` 14–16 | SALARY only if description matches `SALARY` / `"salary"` / `SAL_IMPS` keywords |
| `HDFC.py` 124 | Special case: TRANSFER + description `^[0-9]{6}$` + CREDIT + SAVINGS → SALARY (**exactly 6 digits only**) |
| `SalaryDetection.py` 50 | Requires `partyName` length > 0 — pure numeric narrations usually leave `partyName=""` |
| `HDFC.py` 261 | Blanks partyName if no letters: `[A-Za-z]` false → `""` |
| `ICICI.py` 233 | Blanks partyName matching `[0-9]{6,}` |
| `Axis.py` 168 | Blanks `^[0-9]{4,}$` party names |

So long numeric codes never hit HDFC’s 6-digit salary rule, never match Purpose salary keywords, and cannot enter salary clustering without a party name.

**Obvious fix targets:** widen/narrow cheque remark length rules; add salary path for bare numeric credits (or keep CHEQUE only for short cheque-number lengths and route long refs to TRANSFER + salary heuristics without requiring partyName).

---

### Bug 2 — Narration starts with direction word → empty/wrong counterparty

| Location | Issue |
|----------|--------|
| **`ICICI.py:159`** | `pat="TRFR (TO\|FROM):(.*)"` with **`index=0`** → captures `TO`/`FROM`, not the name (`index=1`). Strong bug. |
| `SBI.py:181,190` + `BankRegexConstants.TRF_STOP_WORDS` | `Transfer To.*` / `Transfer From.*` / `^To Transfer.*` can wipe the **entire** party string |
| `SBI.py:174–176` | Clears partyName when it looks like `^Transfer`, `^Imps`, etc. |
| `HDFC.py:256–257` | Strips `Trf To` / `Paid To` / `Trf ` — incomplete coverage of variants |
| `HDFC.py:106` `HDFC_CLEAN1` | Includes bare `transfer` → can empty names containing that word |
| `Axis.py:167,181` | `TRANSFER TO ` / `Trf From ` strip only some forms |
| `UnionBank.py:118–121,144` | `^TRF? TO`, `^TO [A-Z]`, post-clean `Transfer\|^To` |
| `Karnataka.py:87` | `^To ` extract |
| `RBL.py:137` | Clears `^FROM$` |
| `ICICI.py:201–203,231–232` | IMPS “ To ” handling — order/type dependent |

Direction-prefix narrations that don’t hit the right strip/extract rule leave counterparty empty or set to “To”/“From”/“Transfer”.

---

### Bug 3 — Slash-delimited bill transfer: numeric ref becomes name

Pattern shape: `type/sub-type/numericRef/payeeName`

| Location | Issue |
|----------|--------|
| **`Axis.py:146–147`** | TRANSFER with 1–2 `/` → `sep_by_(…, 0, 1)` = **first** segment, not last name |
| **`ICICI.py:147–151`** | `BIL/...` uses fixed indices (2–5); wrong slot on variant layouts |
| **`ICICI.py:206`** | If extracted party is all digits, retries index 3–4 — still can pick another ref |
| **`ICICI.py:233`** | Any partyName with **6+ digits** blanked (except CMS/IFT) — can destroy names that include refs, or leave only the numeric segment if that was chosen first |
| `HDFC.py:201` | TRANSFER with exactly one `/` → `sep_by_(…, 1, 2)` = second token only |
| `AppUtil.sep_by_` | `split('/')[n1:n2].join('')` — no “last non-numeric segment” helper |
| Kotak bill-pay patterns (`BILL_PAY_KOTAK*`) | Fixed extract groups; fragile to extra slash fields |

No shared “take last alphabetic slash segment” helper; each bank hardcodes index.

---

### Bug 4 — Offsetting credit after matching debit labeled bounce, not reversal

**Adjacent debit→credit same amount logic:**

```98:99:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
[... CREDIT after DEBIT, same amount, desc.eq(shift(2)), channel IMPS|NEFT|UPI|RTGS] → REVERSAL
[... CREDIT after DEBIT, same amount, desc.eq(shift(1))] → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE
```

```49:50:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py
[... same amount, same description, channel IMPS|NEFT|UPI|RTGS] → REVERSAL
[... same amount, same description] → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE
```

Also:
- `StandardCharted.py:60` — same pattern only for `NACH DR IW` → bounce  
- `Saraswat.py:20` — REVERSAL only when channel keywords present (no bounce fallback)  
- `DCB.py:16` — similar shift for NEFT return  

**Problems:**
1. **HDFC REVERSAL uses `shift(periods=2)`** for description equality while bounce uses `shift(1)` — likely off-by-one; many true reversals fail the REVERSAL rule and fall into bounce.
2. **Any** same-amount credit immediately after a debit with the same narration becomes **AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE** unless the channel keyword path wins — so manual transfer reversals / non-NACH offsets are mislabeled bounce.
3. No check that the prior debit was actually AUTO_PAYMENT / NACH / ECS before calling it a bounce.

---

## Key functions cheat sheet

| Concern | Functions / files |
|---------|-------------------|
| Category assignment | `categorize_*_transactions` in each BankScript |
| Payee extraction | Same bank scripts + `sep_by_*` / `py_extract` in AppUtil |
| Sub-tags (salary, loan, bounce type) | `Purpose.purpose`, bank-level subcategory blocks |
| Merchant canonical names | `CleanName.clean_names` |
| Salary frequency logic | `SalaryDetection.salary_detection` |
| Bounce vs reversal pairing | HDFC 98–99, ICICI 49–50, SCB 60, Saraswat 20 |
| Bounce reason subtypes | Purpose 145–147 + `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` / `INSUFF_BOUNCE` |
| Self transfer | `InternalPayment.internal_payment` |
| PFM | `PFMCategorization.pfm_categorization` |

---

## Pipeline order (Controller)

For each bank (example HDFC path conceptually):

`bank_categorize` → (`card_*` if CC) → `purpose` → `clean_names` → `internal_payment` → `salary_detection` (SAVING) → optional PFM

So bank category/party bugs propagate into purpose and salary detection; fixing party extraction early matters most for bugs 2–3, bank category rules for bugs 1 and 4.

---

## Highest-signal fix sites (summary)

1. **Numeric cheque vs transfer vs salary:** cheque `remark` length rules across Axis/PNB/Kotak/YES/UCO/BOM; HDFC salary `^[0-9]{6}$` only; Purpose salary keyword-only; salary_detection requiring partyName.  
2. **Direction words:** ICICI `TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)` wrong capture index; SBI `TRF_STOP_WORDS` over-greedy; incomplete To/From strippers in HDFC/Axis.  
3. **Slash bills:** Axis TRANSFER `sep_by_(0,1)`; ICICI BIL fixed indices + digit-blanking at 233; no last-name-segment helper.  
4. **Bounce vs reversal:** HDFC `shift(2)` vs `shift(1)`; ICICI/HDFC catch-all same-amount credit → `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` without requiring ACH/NACH context.
</task_result>
</task>

The bug is clear: the current `TRF_STOP_WORDS` regexes are too aggressive—they match the entire narration string when it starts with a direction word, so `replace` strips the whole thing and leaves the counterparty name empty.

The fix is to make the stop-word patterns only match the prefix, not the rest of the string. For example:

- Change `Transfer To.*` → `Transfer To ` (trailing space keeps the name)
- Change `Transfer From.*` → `Transfer From `
- Change `^To Transfer.*` → `^To Transfer `
- Change `^By Transfer.*` → ` ^By Transfer `
- Change `^Trf ` → `^Trf ` (already good)
- Change `Funds? Transfer` → `Funds? Transfer ` (trailing space)

That way the direction word is removed but the name stays.

steps.reasoning_content:
Found a clear bug! HDFC uses `accountType=="SAVINGS"` but the rest of the system uses `"SAVING"`. So the salary rule for bare 6-digit codes NEVER fires!
The HDFC cheque rule is broken in two ways at once: the length check is off-by-one and the pattern is too narrow. The current condition can never match because `len()==15` and `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` is 16 characters, so nothing ever triggers “CHEQUE DEPOSIT” for HDFC.

The simplest fix that keeps the spirit of the rule (long numeric remark that looks like a cheque) is to change the length to 16 and keep the existing pattern, or switch to `len().eq(15)` and tighten the pattern to `^[0]{10}[0- 9]{5}`. Either way it will catch the 15- or 16-digit zero-padded numbers users are seeing.

For the salary rule, the accountType mismatch is the real blocker: HDFC returns `"SAVINGS"` while the rest of the system expects `"SAVING"`. That rule will never fire until the string is normalised.

The other three bugs you listed are also straightforward:

- ICICI transfers: the narration starts with a direction word (“From”, “To”, etc.) followed by the counterparty name. The current split logic eats the direction word and leaves the name empty. Changing the split index from  0 to 1 (or using `str.split(maxsplit=1)`) fixes it without touching normal transfers.

- ICICI bill/invoice references: the slash-delimited format is four fields, not three.
